slots.prompt_rule: Five rows of four or five numbers in order up to 100, each with one blank (__) to fill. Answer: the missing number.
Five series (count on by 1, 2, 5 or 10, or count back by 1) with two blanks each; 1 mark per blank. Answer: both numbers.

Five items, each a picture of 1 to 10 of one book object (picture: {kind:"count", name, n}) or dots ({kind:"dots", n}). The instruction asks the question; the item needs no stem. Answer: n. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.
Five pairs of numbers up to 100 written "34 ☐ 43". Answer: the sign.

slots.instruction_en: Read the story and solve. Show your working.
slots.prompt_rule: Five one-step addition stories from the book, sums up to 20, one or two short sentences a Grade 1 child can read. Answer: the number sentence and the sum. The key pays the number: any correct working earns it (a number sentence, counting or a drawing); never write "writes the number sentence" or the unit as a requirement, the paper only says "Show your working".

slots.instruction_en: Read the story and solve. Show your working.
slots.prompt_rule: Five one-step take-away stories from the book, numbers up to 20. Answer: the number sentence and the difference. The key pays the number: any correct working earns it (a number sentence, counting or a drawing); never write "writes the number sentence" or the unit as a requirement, the paper only says "Show your working".

slots.instruction_en: Write the name of each shape.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items, each one shape the book teaches (circle, square, triangle, rectangle, oval, star, heart) drawn as picture: {kind:"shapes", shapes:[{shape}]}. The item needs no stem. Answer: the name. Never the same shape twice. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

Five compare items from the book's measurement pages (longer/shorter, taller/shorter, heavier/lighter, more/less). Each carries picture: {kind:"scene", describe} naming two objects of different kinds side by side that lie straight, standing or lying on one base line with a gap between them, never one above, under or overlapping the other, e.g. "a pencil and a crayon"; never two of the same thing; never ribbon, rope, string or anything that curls. Stem asks which is longer/heavier etc. Answer: the object, named as in the describe and without a size word ("the pencil", never "the long pencil"). The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

lines_en: One mark per correct item unless the paper says otherwise. Spelling is not marked unless the key says so.
